learn.routine: **Learning routine:** read the idea, make one deliberate change, then explain what changed using examples from the current data.
learn.try_body: Start with the default settings. Change **one** control at a time, compare the output, and record what changed and what stayed stable. Use the displayed examples or downloadable output to check whether the pattern answers your actual question.
learn.discuss_body: Ask: *What does this output support? What does it not prove? Which data, language, sampling, or privacy choices could change the result?* Treat every chart as evidence to investigate—not an automatic finding.

home.title: Welcome to TALA
home.intro:
**TALA — Text And Location Analytics** is a hands-on training app that pairs classic **Natural Language Processing** with a full **geospatial** workflow, so participants can move from raw comments to *what people are saying* **and** *where they are saying it*.

*Tala* is Filipino for **star** and for a **record / note** — fitting for a tool that turns notes into insight.
home.text_list:
- Cleaning & Filipino/Taglish stopwords
- Word clouds & frequencies
- VADER sentiment + NRC emotions
- N-grams & co-occurrence networks
- LDA topics + stability
- RAKE keywords, nouns/POS
- Readability metrics & TF-IDF themes
home.geo_list:
- Ingest + **CRS/bounds validation**
- DBSCAN clustering (+ k-distance)
- Grid / centroid generalization
- Philippines land clipping
- Interactive & publication maps
- **NLP per cluster** (privacy-safe)
- GeoJSON / PNG / CSV exports
home.tip: Go to **Text Analytics → Data & Preprocessing** to upload your own data or adjust the text column, then explore the Text and Geospatial sections in the sidebar. Use the sidebar toggles to change the palette, add Filipino stopwords, or hide the Learn panels during assessments.
text_1_data.title: Data & Preprocessing
text_1_data.blurb: Load a dataset, pick the text/coordinate columns, and preview the cleaning pipeline that every text page uses.
text_1_data.uploader: Upload CSV or Excel (.xlsx). Needs a text column; optional `lon`/`lat` for the geospatial pages.
text_1_data.activated: Dataset activated. It now drives every Text and Geospatial page.
text_1_data.sw_caption: Active stopword set: **{count}** words (English + {tagalog}custom). Adjust in the sidebar.
text_2_wordcloud.title: Word Frequency & Clouds
text_2_wordcloud.blurb: The most frequent words after cleaning, shown as a word cloud and a ranked bar chart, plus NRC positive/negative word clouds.
text_2_wordcloud.no_tokens: No tokens to display for the current data / stopwords.
text_2_wordcloud.nrc_missing: The NRC lexicon (nrclex) is unavailable, so polarity word clouds are skipped. Install `nrclex` to enable them.
text_3_sentiment.title: Sentiment & Emotion
text_3_sentiment.blurb: VADER polarity per comment (positive / neutral / negative) and the NRC emotion profile of the corpus.
text_3_sentiment.nrc_missing: NRC emotions require `nrclex`. Install it to enable this chart.
text_3_sentiment.teaching_note: **Teaching note:** VADER and the NRC lexicon are English-tuned. On Filipino/Taglish text they still give a useful signal but will miss or misread native-language emotion — a great point to discuss with participants and to motivate multilingual models.
text_4_ngrams.title: N-grams & Networks
text_4_ngrams.blurb: The most frequent multi-word phrases, and a network of which words appear next to which.
text_4_ngrams.none: No n-grams at this setting — try lowering the minimum document frequency.
text_4_ngrams.no_bigrams: Not enough bigrams to draw a network.
text_5_topics.title: Topic Modeling (LDA)
text_5_topics.blurb: Latent Dirichlet Allocation extracts hidden themes as word distributions, with representative quotes and a stability check.
text_5_topics.not_enough: Not enough documents to fit LDA at this setting.
text_5_topics.stab_caption: LDA is stochastic. We re-fit under different random seeds and measure how consistently the same topics reappear (higher = more stable).
text_5_topics.stab_none: Could not compute stability for this corpus.
text_6_keywords.title: Keywords & Nouns
text_6_keywords.blurb: RAKE keyword extraction, noun / proper-noun ranking (NLTK POS), and a term co-occurrence heatmap.
text_6_keywords.rake_missing: RAKE requires `rake-nltk` (and NLTK data). Install it to enable this.
text_6_keywords.nltk_missing: Noun extraction needs the NLTK tagger data, which is downloaded on first use. Check this container's network access and reload.
text_6_keywords.sample_caption: Computed on a sample of up to 4,000 comments for responsiveness.
text_6_keywords.co_none: Not enough shared terms to build a co-occurrence matrix.
text_7_metrics.title: Linguistic Metrics
text_7_metrics.blurb: Corpus-level readability and lexical-diversity measures, plus the part-of-speech makeup of the text.
text_7_metrics.what_body:
- **Flesch Reading Ease** — higher (up to ~100) is easier to read.
- **Flesch-Kincaid / Gunning Fog / SMOG** — approximate US school grade level needed to understand the text; lower is simpler.
- **Type-Token Ratio** and **Herdan's C** — lexical diversity (vocabulary richness); higher means more varied wording.
text_7_metrics.nltk_missing: POS proportions need the NLTK tagger data, which is downloaded on first use. Check this container's network access and reload.
text_7_metrics.sample_caption: Computed on a sample of up to 4,000 comments.
text_8_themes.title: Themes (TF-IDF K-Means)
text_8_themes.blurb: Group comments into themes with TF-IDF + K-Means, then read each theme's top terms and sentiment mix.
text_8_themes.not_enough: Not enough documents to cluster at this setting.
geo_1_ingest.title: Ingest & CRS Validation
geo_1_ingest.blurb: Build spatial points from the coordinates, validate them, and reproject to a metric CRS — the foundation for every geo step.
geo_1_ingest.no_geo: The active dataset has no longitude/latitude columns. Set them on **Text Analytics → Data & Preprocessing**.
geo_1_ingest.gone: The active dataset is no longer available. Re-upload it on **Text Analytics → Data & Preprocessing**.
geo_1_ingest.crs_caption: Auto-selected projected CRS for metric distances: **EPSG:{epsg}** (UTM zone from the median longitude).
geo_1_ingest.map_caption: Note: at this stage only global lon/lat bounds are enforced — obviously wrong points outside the Philippines are still shown, on purpose.
geo_2_cluster.title: Clustering (DBSCAN)
geo_2_cluster.blurb: Find dense groups of points with DBSCAN, using the k-distance elbow to choose a defensible eps.
geo_2_cluster.need_points: Run **Geospatial → Ingest & CRS Validation** first to build points.
geo_2_cluster.kdist_head: 📈 k-distance plot (find the elbow for eps)
geo_2_cluster.kd_title: Look for the 'knee' — that distance is a good eps
geo_2_cluster.no_clusters: No clusters at this setting — lower min_samples or raise eps.
geo_2_cluster.success: Clusters ready. Continue to **Generalization**, **NLP per Cluster**, or **Map & Exports**.
geo_3_generalize.title: Generalization
geo_3_generalize.blurb: Summarize points into coarser features so patterns read at a glance and individual locations are not exposed.
geo_3_generalize.need_points: Build points (Ingest) — and ideally clusters (DBSCAN) — first.
geo_3_generalize.need_clusters: Cluster centroids need DBSCAN clusters. Run **Clustering** first.
geo_4_map.title: Map & Exports
geo_4_map.blurb: Clip to Philippine land (removing the bogus off-PH coordinates), explore the interactive map, and export the stable output contract.
geo_4_map.need: Build points and clusters first (Ingest → Clustering).
geo_4_map.no_land: Land boundary unavailable; showing unclipped points.
geo_5_nlp.title: NLP per Cluster
geo_5_nlp.blurb: The integration point: profile each spatial cluster with TF-IDF keywords + VADER sentiment — showing aggregates only, never raw text.
geo_5_nlp.no_text: The clustered layer has no text column to analyze.
geo_5_nlp.privacy: 🔒 **Privacy-safe by design:** the table and map expose only cluster-level keywords and sentiment percentages — never individual comments.
geo_5_nlp.map_head: #### Map — cluster centroids with topics & sentiment
